The war wall

All ten papers, in exam order.

Tap a paper to open its file — module checklist, the exact ESE score you need, and its mock tests. The ring shows days left; the bar shows how much of the syllabus you've ticked off.

Revision queue

Study this first.

Nearest paper first, least-ready first. When two papers share a day, the morning paper comes first — 28 December is a double-exam day.

Formula flashcards

Seventeen cards. Tap to flip.

One formula per card, from the papers themselves. Flip a card to see the formula — then flip it back and say it from memory before you peek again.

Mock tests

Practise like it's the real paper.

Log every mock you write — previous-year papers, three hours, 100 marks. The line on the chart is 40: the minimum ESE score. Anything under it is a paper you would fail today.

Know the rules

Six things worth knowing before you sit down.

Where the dates come from: the revised KTU examination calendar published 16 Nov 2026 (S1/S2 dates + S3/S4 slots). The official subject-wise timetable is still the final word — check it against your hall ticket when it lands. HUT300's date (Mon 28 Dec, afternoon) is deduced from its slot, not confirmed — that is why it carries a "to confirm" flag. ESE pass rule, 2019 scheme: at least 40 in the end-semester paper and at least 75 out of 150 overall. Grade boundaries are on the S1/S2 result scale.
